raw_case_text:
A 50-year-old man without any medical conditions was admitted to our hospital with pneumonia caused by COVID-19. Although he was treated with glucocorticoids, his respiratory status deteriorated. Mechanical ventilation was initiated on day 7 after onset of COVID-19 symptoms, and extracorporeal membrane oxygenation support was provided on day 9. Subsequently, his respiratory condition improved, and tracheostomy was performed on day 20 after onset. He was transferred to another hospital for rehabilitation with a tracheostomy. He experienced diarrhea before the transfer on day 43 after the onset of COVID-19, which gradually worsened to 6,000-7,000 mL/day after the transfer; accordingly, he was transferred back to our hospital.
The patient was transferred to our hospital on day 62 after the onset of COVID-19 symptoms. When admitted to our hospital, he had watery diarrhea but no bloody stools. On physical examination, he had a temperature of 36.5 C, a pulse rate of 117 beats per minute, and a blood pressure of 120/83 mm Hg. His weight before the onset of COVID-19 was 114.5 kg (body mass index, 36.5 kg/m2), which decreased to 94.6 kg at the time of readmission to our hospital. Contrast-enhanced computed tomography revealed severe edema of the colon and intestinal fluid accumulation of the entire small bowel (shown in Fig. 1a). Blood tests revealed anemia (hemoglobin, 6.3 g/dL), severe hypoalbuminemia (albumin, 1.0 g/dL), mildly elevated d-dimer levels (3.1 mug/mL), and markedly elevated IL-6 levels (62.6 pg/mL). Stool tests were negative for Clostridioides difficile toxin A/B and glutamate dehydrogenase. Moreover, stool cultures were negative for causative bacteria of enterocolitis, including pathogenic Escherichia coli and Clostridioides difficile. Esophagogastroduodenoscopy revealed villous enlargement and ring-like erosions in the duodenum (shown in Fig. 1b). Capsule endoscopy revealed ring-shaped and multiple map-like ulcerations with villous enlargement in the entire small bowel and duodenum (shown in Fig. 1c). Colonoscopy revealed extensive mucosal edema and multiple shallow map-like ulcerations throughout the colorectal mucosa (shown in Fig. 1d, e). Examination of a biopsy specimen of colonic and small bowel mucosa revealed regenerative changes in the superficial epithelium and inflammatory cell infiltration in the mucosal layer. A PCR test for SARS-CoV-2 in the colonic mucosa was negative. No findings suggested vasculitis, thrombus formation, or inflammatory bowel disease in the biopsy specimens. The biopsy specimens revealed nuclear inclusion bodies. Moreover, immunohistochemistry was positive for the cytomegalovirus (CMV) antigen. In addition to the histological examination, a blood test revealed the presence of the CMV pp65 antigen C7HRP (7 pp65 antigen positive/100,000 white blood cells). The patient was diagnosed with enterocolitis caused by a CMV infection and treated with ganciclovir on day 5 after transfer to our hospital; however, the diarrhea did not improve. A progress chart is shown in Figure 2. We suspected enterocolitis associated with COVID-19 and attempted treatment with a methylprednisolone pulse (intravenous injection, 1,000 mg/day for 3 days) on day 10 after transfer based on a report of a severe diarrhea case in post-COVID-19, similar to GVHD, reported by Ozawa et al.. The severity of diarrhea markedly improved after methylprednisolone administration. Secular changes in endoscopic images of the sigmoid colon are presented in Figure 3a-d. Blood tests were negative for C7HRP on day 14, and IL-6 decreased to 22.6 pg/mL on day 43. After tapering the PSL dose to 15 mg/day, the patient was transferred back to the referral center on day 49 after the transfer. The patient was weaned from PSL and discharged without any diarrhea flare-ups. One year has passed since the termination of steroid administration, and he has had no recurrence of diarrhea.

subjective.chief_complaint: A 50-year-old man presented on day 62 after COVID-19 onset with severe, high-output watery diarrhea (6,000-7,000 mL/day) and a 20 kg weight loss.
subjective.history_of_present_illness: Previously healthy, the patient was hospitalized for severe COVID-19 pneumonia requiring glucocorticoids, mechanical ventilation (day 7), VV-ECMO (day 9), and tracheostomy (day 20) before transfer to a rehabilitation facility. On day 43 after COVID-19 onset, he developed watery diarrhea that progressively worsened to 6,000-7,000 mL/day with a weight loss from 114.5 kg to 94.6 kg, prompting transfer back to our hospital on day 62.
subjective.past_medical_history: Severe COVID-19 pneumonia status post mechanical ventilation, ECMO, and tracheostomy; baseline obesity (pre-illness weight 114.5 kg, BMI 36.5 kg/m2); no other prior medical conditions.
subjective.review_of_systems: Positive for high-volume watery diarrhea (6,000-7,000 mL/day) and 19.9 kg weight loss; negative for bloody stools.

objective.physical_examination: On readmission (day 62): temperature 36.5 °C, heart rate 117 bpm, blood pressure 120/83 mmHg, weight 94.6 kg (down from 114.5 kg).
objective.routine_investigations: Hemoglobin 6.3 g/dL, severe hypoalbuminemia (albumin 1.0 g/dL), mildly elevated D-dimer (3.1 ug/mL), and markedly elevated serum IL-6 (62.6 pg/mL, decreasing to 22.6 pg/mL on day 43). Stool Clostridioides difficile toxin A/B, GDH, and bacterial stool cultures (including pathogenic E. coli) were negative.
objective.advanced_workup: Contrast-enhanced abdominal CT showed severe colonic wall edema and fluid accumulation throughout the small bowel. EGD, capsule endoscopy, and colonoscopy revealed duodenal and pan-small-bowel villous enlargement with ring-like and multiple map-like ulcerations, plus extensive colorectal mucosal edema and shallow map-like ulcerations. Small bowel and colonic mucosal biopsies showed superficial epithelial regenerative changes, mucosal inflammatory infiltration, intranuclear inclusion bodies, and positive CMV antigen immunohistochemistry (colonic tissue SARS-CoV-2 PCR negative; no vasculitis, thrombosis, or IBD). Peripheral blood CMV pp65 antigenemia (C7-HRP) was positive at 7 pp65-positive cells per 100,000 WBCs (negative by day 14).

assessment_and_plan.assessment_and_confirmation: Diagnosed with severe post-COVID-19 GVHD-like enterocolitis complicated by cytomegalovirus (CMV) enterocolitis (confirmed by nuclear inclusion bodies and positive CMV IHC on small bowel/colonic biopsies and positive peripheral blood C7-HRP CMV pp65 antigenemia of 7/100,000 WBCs; C. difficile, bacterial enteropathogens, and tissue SARS-CoV-2 ruled out). Intravenous ganciclovir initiated on transfer day 5 cleared blood C7-HRP antigenemia by day 14 but failed to reduce diarrhea volume; addition of pulse intravenous methylprednisolone (1,000 mg/day for 3 days on day 10) followed by a prednisolone taper resulted in marked resolution of diarrhea and mucosal healing on serial sigmoidoscopies. Transferred back to rehabilitation on day 49 on prednisolone 15 mg/day, subsequently weaned off steroids completely with no recurrence of diarrhea at 1-year follow-up.
